what_happened: The operator ran three jobs (bwhh, k0w6 and w314) directly, ahead of the order in Athena's plan. The plan still gave every rung the default implementation type, so the speed items the owner had named as top priority would have run last. The operator overrode the plan by hand. This is the third such override of the plan's order.
cause: Planning still does not take the owner's stated priority as an input. It sequences rungs by their default work type. No check compares the plan's order with the owner's latest priority. The queue has no priority support either, so the only way to change order is for the operator to bypass the plan. Gap k0w6 was logged twice but not fixed, so the same bypass keeps recurring. Logging a gap did not lead to a fix being scheduled.
prevention: Make the owner's current priority list a required, recorded input to planning. Plan ordering must sort by it before sorting by default rung or type. Add a code check at plan time that fails or flags any plan where an item matching a stated priority sits behind lower-priority items. Add a priority field to queue items so the drain honors that order without operator bypass. Schedule the k0w6 fix ahead of other work, since it has already caused repeat overrides.
proposed_request: Make Athena's plan ordering follow the owner's stated priority. (1) Record the owner's current priorities, taken from addenda, as an input to planning. (2) Order plan rungs by that priority first and by default work type second. (3) Add a plan-time check that reports an error when an item matching a stated priority is sequenced after items that do not match. (4) Give queue items a priority value that the drain respects. Done when a plan built with speed as the owner's top priority puts the speed items first, the check fails on a plan that does not, and the drain runs a higher-priority item before older lower-priority ones. This resolves gap k0w6.
